transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm a firefighter, and I've recently taken on more leadership responsibilities and promotional coursework to become a captain. But I'm really struggling because when I’m not on an actual call, I just can’t keep my attention on training, reports, or manuals long enough to get through them properly.
Have you struggled with focus and attention like this since childhood, or is this a new issue that only started with your recent promotion and coursework?

It’s really come to a head and been impossible to ignore over the last year and a half with this coursework, but it's definitely not new. Even back in elementary school, my teachers had to move my seat because I wouldn't stop talking, and my report cards always said I was smart but couldn't sit still or focus. I'd even do my homework and then completely forget to turn it in.
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about a variety of different things in your daily life, and is this worry difficult to control?

No, I wouldn't say I have constant, uncontrollable worry about everyday things in general. I'm definitely stressed and deeply concerned about my recent mistakes at work and losing my shot at the promotion, but it doesn't feel like a general anxiety about everything else.
Do these struggles with focus, forgetfulness, or restlessness also affect your home life, daily chores, or relationships, or are they mostly limited to your work and studying?

It definitely spills over into my home life, and honestly, I feel pretty embarrassed about how it affects my family. I constantly forget to call my wife back or pay bills left right on the counter, and I can't even sit through a movie with my son without constantly fidgeting or getting up. Even waiting in a simple line at the store feels like absolute torture because I get so impatient.
